profile.headline: Software Engineer II at AWS S3
profile.summary: A recent graduate of Bowdoin College with a double major in Computer Science and Government, I have prior experience building scalable, production-quality backend systems. Recently worked as a research fellow on a project that utilizes both computational game theory and various machine learning techniques, such as generative models, to predict Senate voting behavior. In the last year, our research has led to several peer-reviewed publication, a large NSF grant, and the Bowdoin College Computer Science Research Prize.

positions.title: Game Theory Research Fellow
positions.description:
• Worked on ML project to infer Senate influence networks. Utilizes computational Game Theory to compute Nash Equilibrium predictions of voting behavior and identify sets of influential senators.
• Applied ML techniques (Fuzzy C-Mean, Generative Models) to identify clusters of bills from context
• Decreased computation time (hours to minutes) and the number of computed Nash Equilibrium joint action solutions (millions to thousands) by incorporating contextual data
• Performed bootstrapping and nested CV to optimize hyperparameters and evaluate model accuracy
• Streamlined dataset collection/parsing and model learning through Python scripting
• Extended computational framework through Probabilistic Graphical Models and Expectation Maximization
• Applied modularity and network metrics to evaluate polarization within bill clusters
• Co-authored journal paper that was accepted to multiple international conferences 
• Leveraged Knowledge in Python (scikit-learn, graphviz, networkx modules), MATLAB, LaTeX

positions.title: Game Theory Honors Thesis
positions.description:
• Applied the ideal-point LIG model to examine voting patterns and influence networks in the US Senate
• Studied the effect of bill polarity on the computed set of Nash Equilibrium and Most Influential Sets
• Laid the groundwork for extending our computational framework through Probabilistic Graphical Models

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
• Led the design and development of a RESTful web service application for the Collections Library
• Built scalable bento-style search service that consolidates results to improve accessibility
• Reduced UX load time from 5 to 2 seconds by implementing algorithm to incrementally request data
• Collaborated on the execution of load testing on new student portal using Locust.io framework
• Managed and debugged RideShare and ShuttleApp student transportation applications
• Leveraged Knowledge in Full Stack Web Development, programmed in Java using Spring Boot,
JavaScript, SQL Server, AJAX, Jackson JSON, Locust, and debugged using Chrome Developer Tools

projects.title: Discover Daily: Web Application built on Spotify API
projects.description:
• Incorporating backend database to automate weekly update of user’s Top Tracks playlist
• Developed web application to create unique playlists based on user recommendations
• Utilized: Flask (with sessions/request packages), Jinja, SQLite, HTML/Bootstrap, AJAX, Virtualenv

projects.title: Socket Based Chat Application
projects.description:
• Developed a multithreaded chat server that enables clients to communicate over local networks
• Integrated SQL backend database to persistently store user information and accounts
• Utilized: Java, Socket (IP/TCP) Programming, MySQL, Swing, JFrame GUI, Multithreading

publications.title: Spheres of Legislation: Polarization and Most Influential Nodes in Behavioral Context

organizations.name: Achon Uganda Children's Fund
organizations.description:
• Conceptualized three week long global trip in connection with Achon Uganda Children’s Fund
• Spearheaded, and student lead, trip of ten students to examine post-genocidal Rwanda/Uganda
• Brought Julius Achon (founder AUCF) to Catlin Gabel School community to raise awareness for his grassroots projects to improve health care in Northern Uganda
• Served as fundraising spokesperson at Portland running events
• Solicited items to be sold at silent auctions within Portland
